scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Original A1 assessment of Mia's short English reading story; independent wording and situations. Teacher approval pending.

tabs.title: Try It Yourself
tabs.description: Use the ideas in simple situations.

questions.q: Mia sees a difficult sentence. What does she do first?
choices: She closes her book and goes home.
She makes a small mark next to the sentence.
She asks Leo to write the story.
She reads a different book.
questions.explanation: Paragraph one says Mia writes a question mark next to the difficult sentence.

questions.q: What helps Mia understand a word in the story?
choices: A message on her phone.
Her brother's homework.
A long list of answers from Leo.
A picture next to the story.
questions.explanation: Leo shows Mia a picture, which helps her understand one new word.

questions.q: Why does Mia smile on Friday?
choices: Her teacher gives her no reading homework.
She finishes school early that day.
She can understand more of a new story.
Leo reads the new story for her.
questions.explanation: Mia smiles because the new story is easier for her to understand than before.

questions.q: Why does Leo NOT tell Mia all the answers?
choices: He wants Mia to think and learn too.
He does not want to be her friend.
He cannot read the story himself.
He is busy reading a new book.
questions.explanation: Leo supports Mia with a picture while allowing her to work out a meaning.

questions.q: Mia asks about words she does not know. What does this show?
choices: She does not want to practise English.
She can read every word alone.
She is ready to get help with learning.
She thinks books are too easy.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two describes asking about two unfamiliar words and learning from help.

questions.q: How does Mia feel about reading at the end?
choices: She wants to read again.
She wants to stop reading stories.
She only wants to study at school.
She is worried about her next story.
questions.explanation: At the end Mia wants to continue practising and reads at home.

questions.q: Your friend does not know a word in a story. What can you do?
choices: Tell them to stop reading today.
Show them a useful picture or example.
Tell them not to ask any questions.
Give them a new book with no pictures.
questions.explanation: Leo helps Mia with a picture instead of giving every answer.

questions.q: You do not understand one sentence. What is a good idea?
choices: Forget the whole story now.
Read only the last sentence.
Say that you do not like English.
Mark it and ask about it later.
questions.explanation: Mia marks the hard sentence and later asks for help.

questions.q: A new story is still difficult for you. What can you learn from Mia?
choices: You must understand every word today.
You can learn more by practising again.
You should ask a friend to read it all.
You need to get a perfect mark first.
questions.explanation: Mia improves even though the new story is still not easy.

questions.q: Which sentence is true about learning English in the story?
choices: Good students never ask questions.
Only a teacher can help with words.
Reading once is enough for everyone.
Small steps can help you understand more.
questions.explanation: The story shows that a second try, a notebook and questions lead to progress.
